findings:
🔵 [stop-unverified-exit] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `--stop` waits up to 5 s for `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` to vanish but prints "stopped … pid N" and returns 0 even if the writer is still alive (e.g. blocked in a long probe spawnSync so the SIGTERM handler has not run yet). Spec only mandates read-pid → cmdline check → SIGTERM, and the suite's "watcher process is gone after --stop" assertion passes, so not blocking; follow-up: after the wait, if `cmdlineOf(pid)` is still non-null, print "still running" to stderr and return 1.
🔵 [roots-set-unbounded] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `state.roots` only grows, so `<key>--<root>.json` files for roots that disappear from the collector are rewritten forever with `runs: []` on every publish. Harmless for P1a correctness (readers get an empty, correctly scoped envelope) and the plan does not define scope-file retirement; leave for the P3 idle/retention work.
🔵 [flock-version-probe] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `flockAvailable()` requires `flock --version` to exit 0; busybox flock lacks `--version` and would yield `flock_unavailable` on a system where locking works. Plan targets util-linux flock explicitly, so excluded; a cheaper probe is `flock -n <tmpfile> true`.
